title: 1003-abstention-under-label-shift-framework
universal_lens: The abstention operator acts as a non-linear filter on the calibrated probability simplex. By substituting posterior probabilities for latent labels under covariate shift, it constructs an optimal decision boundary that maximizes a chosen utility functional while strictly bounding the exposure to high-entropy regions of the feature space.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps calibrated posteriors p(y|x) to conformal prediction sets. The label-shift adaptation (Saerens et al.) dynamically recalibrates base rates as season priors drift. Abstention corresponds to rejecting events where the conformal p-value falls below a dynamic threshold, ensuring strict coverage guarantees despite distributional shifts in team performance.
gse_mapping: In GSE, the no-bet filter is a state-transition gate. Instead of maximizing accuracy, the engine optimizes realized betting metrics (e.g., auROC or weighted-kappa) by skipping games. The O(NM) Monte-Carlo optimizer evaluates contiguous intervals of sorted probabilities to find the exact abstention window that yields maximum sensitivity at a fixed specificity.

primitives.name: Calibrated Probability Label Proxy
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions - auROC = (1/(n-n+)) Σi yi si-, with si- = Σ_{i′<i}(1-y_{i′}), n-/n+ class counts — used with calibrated p replacing y.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: y_i: true binary label (dimensionless); s_{i-}: cumulative sum of negative indicators prior to i (dimensionless count); n_-, n_+: class counts (dimensionless); p: calibrated probability proxy for y (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: Calibrated p(y|x) accurately reflects true likelihoods; ranking order of p preserves the ground truth ordering required for ROC analysis.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Severe miscalibration where the monotonic relationship between predicted probability and true outcome probability breaks down, rendering the proxy invalid.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSE's edge-ranking system. Games are sorted by expected value (calibrated p), and the auROC metric measures the separation between winning and losing bets when abstaining on low-confidence edges.
layer2.telemetry: Realized auROC on held-out weekly blocks compared against baseline without abstention.

primitives.name: Weighted Kappa Marginal Gain Optimizer
primitives.verbatim_quote: S=Σi yisi- via running sums); weighted-κ optimizer — O(NC) deterministic marginal-improvement-per-example, abstain on top-k marginal gains (C classes).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: S: subset of examples retained (dimensionless set); f(x): predicted class (dimensionless); W_{i,j}: weight matrix for disagreement between true i and predicted j (dimensionless); N_i: true class counts (dimensionless); F_j: predicted class counts (dimensionless).
primitives.assumptions: The cost of misclassification is captured by the weight matrix W; removing an example only affects the denominator via marginal counts N_i and F_j.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Highly imbalanced datasets where removing a few examples drastically skews the marginal predicted counts F_j, causing the denominator to collapse and kappa to become unstable.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's profit-weighted accuracy filter. The 'marginal gain' of abstaining on a game is equivalent to the increase in overall portfolio Sharpe ratio if that specific bet is removed.
layer2.telemetry: Delta in weighted Cohen's kappa (or profit margin) after iteratively removing the top-k lowest-edge games.

primitives.name: Jensen-Shannon Divergence Information Baseline
primitives.verbatim_quote: Novel baseline introduced: abstain on examples with lowest Jensen–Shannon divergence between predicted probs and prior class probs (prediction ≈ prior ⟹ no information).
primitives.latex: D_{JS}(P || Q) = \frac{1}{2} D_{KL}(P || M) + \frac{1}{2} D_{KL}(Q || M), \quad M = \frac{P+Q}{2}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P: predicted probability distribution p(y|x) (dimensionless); Q: prior class distribution (dimensionless); M: average distribution (dimensionless); D_{KL}: Kullback-Leibler divergence (nats or bits).
primitives.assumptions: The prior Q represents the true base rate of outcomes; minimal divergence implies the model provides zero alpha over the market consensus.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the market prior Q is itself severely misestimated, leading the model to incorrectly abstain on genuinely high-information events that happen to align with the flawed prior.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's 'market efficiency' veto. If our internal model's output distribution is nearly identical to the implied probability distribution from the sportsbook (the prior), the JSD is near zero, triggering an automatic no-bet.
layer2.telemetry: Mean JSD between model outputs and closing line implied probabilities for skipped vs. taken games.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical unification rests on treating abstention not as a failure mode, but as an active optimization variable within a constrained utility maximization problem. By assuming label shift—where p(x|y) remains invariant but the base rate p(y) evolves—we can decouple the calibration of the conditional probability from the estimation of the marginal. The Alexandari et al. framework elegantly substitutes the unknown true labels y with calibrated probabilities p(y|x) in standard performance metrics like auROC and weighted Cohen's kappa. This substitution transforms discrete combinatorial optimization problems into continuous, differentiable landscapes (or efficiently sortable lists). For instance, the O(N) auROC optimizer relies on sorting examples by their calibrated score; the optimal abstention set forms a contiguous interval in this sorted space. Similarly, the weighted-kappa optimizer computes the exact marginal improvement of removing an example in O(NC) time, exploiting the fact that removal only perturbs the global normalization constants. The Jensen-Shannon divergence baseline offers a geometric interpretation: we abstain when the posterior distribution lies too close to the prior manifold, indicating a lack of informational gain. In the context of GSE, these operators form a rigorous 'no-bet' layer. Instead of forcing a binary prediction on every sporting event, the engine calculates the marginal utility of inclusion. If including a game decreases the overall portfolio's sensitivity-at-specificity or degrades the weighted agreement with true outcomes, it is filtered out. The breakdown regime occurs precisely when the calibration assumption fails—if p(y|x) is biased, the proxy labels corrupt the optimization objective, leading to suboptimal or even detrimental abstention decisions. Thus, the robustness of the entire sovereign primitive hinges on the quality of the underlying conformal or Platt scaling calibration.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This framework inherits from the classical theory of selective classification (Chapelle et al.), which sought to minimize error under a rejection constraint. It diverges by explicitly incorporating label shift (Saerens et al., 2000), a concept rooted in empirical Bayes methods for correcting prevalence bias. The use of calibrated probabilities as surrogates for latent variables echoes the EM algorithm's E-step, bridging modern machine learning calibration techniques with foundational statistical decision theory.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From the perspective of the opposing agent—the sportsbook or the market—their pricing models represent the prior distribution Q. Our model generates P. When P closely mirrors Q (low JSD), we recognize that the market has already priced in all available information, leaving no exploitable edge. Conversely, when our calibrated posteriors deviate significantly from the market prior, we identify a cognitive asymmetry. The abstention mechanism acts as a disciplined actor that refuses to engage when the market's collective intelligence matches or exceeds our own, preserving capital for moments of genuine informational advantage.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A critical veto condition arises from data leakage during the calibration phase. If the held-out calibration set is not strictly independent of the test distribution under shift, the estimated p(y|x) will be biased, causing the auROC and kappa optimizers to select abstention intervals based on spurious correlations. Furthermore, the assumption of contiguous abstention intervals in sorted-probability order may fail if the feature space exhibits multi-modal edge distributions that do not align with a single scalar confidence score. We must enforce a strict temporal separation: calibration must occur on historical windows that predate the current evaluation block, and any drift in p(y) must be continuously monitored via conformal residuals to prevent silent degradation of the no-bet filter.
